sources.findings: Documents --help, --version, --registry, -i input and --n-threads. MOOSE applications can customize flags. The three readiness modes do not supply an input file; the separate cube command does.

Version/help and registry branches mark the application ready to exit. Registry source emits five tab-separated columns and separate object/action rows; the caller matches explicit object names rather than arbitrary prose occurrences.

sources.documented_page_version: PETSc3.26.0; not a claim about the future installed library version
sources.findings: The command-line -skip_petscrc option suppresses user/current .petscrc and petscrc options files. The child environment supplies no PETSC_OPTIONS. This is not an OS filesystem sandbox or proof that no other application-specific configuration can exist.

version_scope: The documented modes are source-backed; exact installed help/version/registry support remains a future native observation. A guessed release-tag raw MooseApp.C URL returned404, so no exact package-source revision match is claimed.
native_warning_limit: The completed cube001 reports -skip_petscrc unused. Options-file suppression is not established.

scaling_trial_sources.findings: Documents unit Dirichlet rows versus large kernel Jacobians as a scaling concern; automatic_scaling=true and grouped displacement variables. Default pure Jacobian scaling, computed once. A rationale for a separate trial, not proof of success.

The revision printed by native001 declares automatic_scaling and scaling_group_variables; transfers Jacobian-based scaling controls to nonlinear systems. The installed binary/source equivalence is not independently attested.

AD residual/Jacobian assembly applies the variable scaling factor, while save_in copies unscaled residual entries. Native reaction outputs must still pass the unchanged independent field/reaction tests.
Nodal BC Jacobian insertion explicitly uses scaling factor1 and default unit diagonal. The unchanged assessor still requires24 identity rows.
